title: kbmon's query-log line says how many spool rows wait for delivery, apart from ops rows and rows of ended sessions
goal: kbmon's query-log line splits the spool count it prints (spool_state counts every row) into the rows a delivery will take, the ops rows, and rows of sessions that ended more than a day ago, so '952 rows wait in the spool' no longer sits beside '0 entries undelivered' as if both were pending: on 2026-11-08 about 470 of the 952 were ops rows and some were 15 days old (querylog show --spool). Whether the old rows are stuck is read during the work and filed as its own bug if so.

run: import subprocess,sys;r=subprocess.run([sys.executable,'_tools/kbmon.py','--status','querylog','--timeout','60'],capture_output=True,text=True);sys.exit(r.returncode not in (0,1) or 'rows wait in the spool' in r.stdout)
